title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, from the previous page: for each type (g,ν) Grothendieck considers the Teichmüller groupoid of curves of that type. This is the fundamental groupoid of M_{g,ν} over the base points chosen. Over C it is described topologically. Over an arbitrary algebraically closed field k it is the profinite étale fundamental groupoid. He wants, over any such k, a functor 'bouchage des trous' (filling in a chosen set I of ν' punctures). This functor goes from the type-(g,ν) Teichmüller groupoid to the type-(g,ν−ν') groupoid. In modern terms it is the map on fundamental groupoids induced by the forgetful morphism M_{g,ν} → M_{g,ν−ν'}, which over C is the Birman-type surjection of mapping class groups. He also wants it to be transitive under successive fillings.

The difficulty: in the topological 'isotopy category' over C there are also morphisms given by inclusions of subsurfaces. These compose with the existing arrows. He does not see how to produce algebraic counterparts of these 'inclusion morphisms' that compose with the arrows of the Galois–Teichmüller category. He stresses that this is a category, not a groupoid, so it already has non-invertible arrows.

This page states the fallback and its cost. One could 'y aller comme une brute': define a larger category than the Galois–Teichmüller category, with more arrows, by suitable generators and relations. But then, when the base field is C, it becomes problematic to identify this Galois–Teichmüller category with a 'profinite completion' of the isotopy category considered earlier. A category defined abstractly by generators and relations gives no a priori comparison with the profinite completion of the topological category.

The problem served is building a coherent algebraic and profinite 'Teichmüller tower' on which Gal(Q̄/Q) acts. Its arrows must include both point-forgetting maps and subsurface-inclusion (gluing) maps, compatibly with the topological picture over C. The next page begins a new section, 'Opérations de Γ_{Q̄/Q} sur π1 M_{0,3}'. The page records an obstacle; it does not resolve it.
errors: No mathematical error. The forgetful ('bouchage') functor needs the target type to be stable (2g−2+ν−ν' > 0). It is only well defined on fundamental groupoids once base points are chosen compatibly. Here that is left implicit.

The obstacle about inclusion morphisms is real at this stage. It was later resolved by tangential base points at infinity on the Deligne–Mumford–Knudsen boundary (Ihara–Nakamura) rather than by a bare generators-and-relations definition. Grothendieck here has not yet adopted that viewpoint.

ideas.what: Functor 'bouchage des trous' between Teichmüller groupoids of type (g,ν) and (g,ν−ν'), defined over any algebraically closed field, with transitivity under successive fillings
ideas.modern_name: Forgetful maps M_{g,n+1}→M_{g,n} on (profinite) fundamental groupoids; Birman exact sequence; point-erasing operations in the Teichmüller tower

ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower; operations of 'bouchage' and gluing)

ideas.what: Need for 'inclusion morphisms' (subsurface inclusions) in the algebraic/profinite Galois–Teichmüller category, compatible with the topological isotopy category over C
ideas.modern_name: Gluing/boundary operations of the Teichmüller tower via tangential base points at infinity on the DMK boundary
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §2 (tour de Teichmüller, points base à l'infini)

ideas.what: Defining an enlarged Galois–Teichmüller category by generators and relations, and the problem of identifying it over C with the profinite completion of the topological isotopy category
ideas.modern_name: Profinite completion of presented groupoids/categories; comparison of discrete and profinite Teichmüller towers; Grothendieck–Teichmüller group as automorphisms of the profinite tower

missed.claim: Early (post-1978) record of Grothendieck hitting the obstruction that subsurface-inclusion morphisms have no evident algebraic counterpart in the Galois–Teichmüller category. He also notes that a brute-force presentation by generators and relations breaks the comparison with the profinite completion of the topological category. This is historical context for how the Esquisse's tangential base points at infinity came about, not a new mathematical result.
missed.quote: définir une catégorie plus grosse que la cat. de Galois-Teichmüller ... par générateurs et relations convenables. Mais alors il devient problématique ... d'interpréter cette catégorie de Galois-Teichmüller comme une "complétée profinie" de la catégorie isotopique
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents the genesis of the Teichmüller-tower formalism. It also shows Grothendieck already aware of the presentation-versus-profinite-completion issue later handled by Drinfeld and Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps.

deep.surprise_reason: A short page stating an obstacle and a rejected brute-force workaround. The issues (forgetful maps, gluing via inclusions, profinite comparison) are all well known from the Esquisse and later work. Only the historical detail of this intermediate stage is of mild interest.
